Line x tester analysis

Source: R/breeding.R
line_tester.Rd

Analysis of a line x tester mating design (Kempthorne 1957; Singh and Chaudhary 1985): the analysis of variance of the entries in randomised complete blocks, with the crosses partitioned into lines, testers and their interaction; general combining ability of lines and testers, specific combining ability of the crosses, their standard errors, the proportional contribution of every source to the variation among crosses and the genetic components.

Usage

line_tester(data, response, line, tester, block = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

line, tester

Names of the line (female) and tester (male) columns.

block

Name of the block column (randomised complete blocks); when NULL the entries are taken as completely randomised.

Value

An object of class "ad_line_tester".

Details

A row is a cross when it has both a line and a tester, a line parent when the tester is missing (NA or empty) and a tester parent when the line is missing; parents are optional. Rows with neither (for instance checks) are not used.

Lines and testers are tested against the error and, in the random model of Kempthorne, against the line x tester interaction (anova_lxt). The average covariance of half sibs is [((l-1) MSl + (t-1) MSt) / (l+t-2) - MSlxt] (l+t-2) / (r (2lt - l - t)), the moment estimator under equal variances of lines and testers; sigma2_A = 4 CovHS / (1 + F) and sigma2_D = 4 sigma2_SCA / (1 + F)^2 are given for F = 0 and F = 1. The standard errors of the effects are the usual ones, sqrt(MSE / (r t)) for lines, sqrt(MSE / (r l)) for testers and sqrt(MSE / r) for crosses.

References

Kempthorne, O. (1957) An Introduction to Genetic Statistics. Wiley. Singh, R. K. and Chaudhary, B. D. (1985) Biometrical Methods in Quantitative Genetic Analysis. Kalyani.

Examples

lt <- line_tester(maize_lxt, "Yield_t_ha", "Line", "Tester", block = "Block")
lt
